notes.decision: Translated 'Teaching.' Reading ⲧⲍⲃⲥⲱ as Lycopolitan variant of ⲧⲥⲃⲱ 'the teaching' with epenthetic ⲍ-onset (cf. accumulated vocabulary entry on ⲧϣⲁⲙⲧⲉ ⲛ̄ⲍⲃⲥⲱ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄ rendered 'three Living Teachings' despite literal ϩⲃⲥⲱ 'garment' — the technical use is 'teaching/lesson'). Per terminology rule for ⲥⲃⲱ.

Translated 'her duration' tentatively. ϭⲁⲧ etymology unclear; possibly relates to a Lyc. duration/extent root, or could be a hapax meaning 'flooding/swelling' fitting the Tigris-flood narrative that follows. The doubled ⲧⲉ ⲧⲉ may be scribal dittography. Confidence low; flagged for parallels.

Preserved as 'Concerning' in parentheses. The recurring ⲍ̄ⲁ markers in lines 21-24 appear to function as marginal/rubric repetitions of the chapter-heading particle ⲍⲁ/ⲍⲁⲡⲣⲁ 'concerning' (cf. accumulated vocabulary). They frame the kephalaion title without contributing new content.

Translated 'multiplied, rising up.' ⲁϣⲉⲓⲧⲉ likely from ⲁϣⲁⲓ̈ 'be many, multiply' (cf. accumulated vocabulary ⲁϣⲉⲓⲧⲉ 'multitude/abundance'); ⲧⲟⲛⲱ = ⲧⲱⲟⲩⲛ 'rise up' (3pl perfect). Together describe the river's flood-swell rising under the lions.

Translated 'they sprang forth.' Lyc. reflex possibly of ⲡⲱϩⲧ 'pour forth' or ⲡⲱⲣϣ 'spread.' Confidence low; the verbal series ⲃⲱⲍⲧ̄/ⲃⲣ̄ⲃⲣ̄/6ⲱⲣⲉ describes a crescendo of multiplication-ebullition-strengthening of the lions.

Translated 'flood.' Possibly Lyc. variant of ⲏⲙⲏⲣⲉ/ⲙⲣⲱ 'flood, inundation, riverbank.' Context (Tigris in Pharmouthi/April flood season) supports flood-reading; the lions are pushed out by the great inundation.
Read as ⲛ̄-ⲙⲏⲧⲉ 'in the midst' (Lyc spelling with ⲓ̈ⲙ- for ⲛ̄ⲙ̄- and ⲙⲉⲧⲉ for ⲙⲏⲧⲉ). Mid-clause from preceding page; precise sense uncertain.
Translated 'way/road' from Coptic ⲡⲱⲧ 'race, course, road.' Could alternatively be Greek loan πύλη 'gate' with metathesis. Either fits 'drew them into the X of the city.'

Translated 'his heart.' ⲡⲉϩ- = Lyc 'his' + ⲧⲏⲩ likely for ϩⲏⲧ 'heart' (with metathesis or scribal variation), since 'fear in his X' demands a heart/breast term. Alternative: literal 'his wind/breath' (= ⲡⲧⲏⲩ) used idiomatically for courage/spirit.

Translated 'his other kingship' literally. ⲧⲉϩ- 'his' + ⲕⲉ- 'other' + ⲙⲛⲧⲣⲣⲟ 'kingship.' Sense in narrative obscure — possibly the ruler of a neighboring kingdom rising in alarm at the lion-incursion described in the foregoing.
Translated 'multitude.' Likely Lyc ⲁⲱⲉⲓ̈ⲧⲉ = ⲁϣⲁⲓ̈/ⲁϣⲉⲓ̈ⲧⲉ 'multitude, abundance' (cf. accumulated vocab ⲁϣⲉⲓ̈ⲧⲉ tentative). Modifies 'herd of lions.'

Translated 'they were gazing/looking after.' ⲙⲟⲩϩ here likely a Lyc form with sense of 'attend, watch, look toward,' possibly cognate with ⲙⲟⲩϣⲧ̄ 'examine' or contracted from it. Unusual since ⲙⲟⲩϩ normally = 'fill,' but ⲛⲉⲩⲙⲟⲩϩ ⲡⲉ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁ + object pattern fits a verb of attentive looking.

Translated 'they also leapt forth.' Construction ⲣ̄- ('do') + ⲡⲕⲉ- ('the additional/other') + ⲡⲱϩⲧ ('cast/leap') = 'they did the additional leaping/casting.' Subject 'lions' (continuing from context).

Translated 'her aspect.' ⲡⲉⲥ- 'her' + ϩⲉⲉ likely = Lyc form of ϩⲏ 'face/aspect/manner.' Subject 'she' is the cloak/garment of lions (feminine ⲧϩⲃⲥⲱ) personified as a force of wrath. The '+' marker in ⲡⲉⲥϩⲉ+ⲉ may indicate scribal correction.

Translated 'making it (a great sea)' — taking ⲉⲟⲓⲣⲁϩ as ⲉ-ⲟⲩⲉⲓⲣⲉ-ϥ (circumstantial 'while making it') and ⲟⲓⲣⲟ as related to ⲓⲟⲣⲟ 'great water/expanse' or just an intensifying repetition. The phrase qualifies the river of Tigris becoming a great sea.
Translated 'their multitude.' Possibly = ⲧⲙⲏⲣⲉ + 3pl pronoun-suffix 'their herd' (contracted), or ⲧ-ⲙⲣⲟⲩ 'the harbor'(?). Subject of ⲛⲁⲣ̄ 'shall become' in next line.
Translated as predicate of becoming-many ('how great'). Possibly Lyc reflex of ⲛⲁϣⲉ 'be many' or ⲛ̄ϩⲟⲩⲟ 'in excess.' Recurs in line 26 as ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲁⲧ 'hosts/multitudes' (translated 'hosts' there).
Translated 'uncountable.' Privative ⲛⲁⲧ- + verbal ⲱⲡ 'count' + 3sg.f. suffix -ⲥ̄. Standard Coptic privative idiom 'without counting it' = countless.

Translated 'while desiring to crush.' ⲉⲩ-ⲟⲩⲁⲱⲥ̄ = circumstantial + ⲟⲩⲱϣ-ⲥ̄ 'wanting it.' ⲁⲧⲟⲩⲉⲱⲥ = ⲁ-ⲧⲣⲉⲩ-ⲱⲱⲥ 'to make them crush' (= ⲱⲱⲥ 'beat, crush'). The archons want to crush hosts of light-beings.

Translated 'primordial-ones.' Lexeme uncertain — possibly a Lyc collective for 'first/foremost ones' or 'shadows' (ϩⲁⲓⲃⲉⲥ?), or 'molders/fashioners.' Modified by ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲣⲭⲏ 'of the beginning,' supporting a primordial-being reading.
Translated 'lurked and swallowed.' ⲥⲱϩⲡ̄ = 'lie in wait, lurk, ambush' (= Sah. ⲥⲱⲣⲡ̄/ⲥⲱⲣϩ̄?); ⲱⲙⲕ̄ 'swallow.' The narrative inversion: archons consume the lions (the cloak they were given to wear).
Translated 'bearers' tentatively. Possibly compound on ⲱⲗ 'carry, lift' + ⲁⲗⲱⲓⲣⲉ (unidentified). With ⲙⲡⲧⲉⲕⲟ 'of destruction' suggests instrumental agents of destruction. Confidence low.

Translated 'branch' (of a river). The term recurs lines 1, 8, 28 always with ⲡⲓⲉⲣⲟ 'river' or ⲛ̄ⲛⲥⲧⲟⲓⲭⲉⲓⲟⲛ 'of the elements,' confirming the watercourse-tributary sense (cf. Coptic ⲧⲱⲧ as 'joining/fork' or ⲧⲟⲩⲱⲧ 'channel'). Preserves the hydrographic register central to the chapter's punitive-river vision.
Rendered 'great river of Judgment.' ⲧⲓⲕⲣⲓⲥ = Greek κρίσις with prosthetic ⲧⲓ-. Capitalized as cosmic principle: this is the underworld punitive river that pours fire into the mouths of bound archons.

Translated 'down' (toward the archons' mouths). ⲁϩⲣⲏⲓ̈ in Lycopolitan/Sahidic can denote either upward or downward; the punitive context (river pouring into mouths to burn) requires the downward reading. The bound archons are 'upon the land of Death' (line 20), so the river descends to them.

Translated 'they continually burn them' — ϣⲁ- habitual + ⲣⲁⲭϩ (Lyc. = ⲣⲱⲕϩ̄ 'burn,' cf. ⲣⲱⲭⲍ̄ in vocabulary) + 3pl object. The verb pairs with ⲣⲱⲭϩ̄ 'his burning' in line 5, confirming the burning-judgment register.
Translated 'marvel/wonder.' Lyc. ⲣⲱⲡⲏⲣⲉ = ϣⲡⲏⲣⲉ 'wonder, marvel.' Recurs lines 11, 14, 29 — the elect one's marveling response to the apostle's revelation about the river of Judgment.

Translated 'prison' rather than 'destruction.' In context with 'mighty boundary' and the bound/blackened/buried archons (line 18), the carceral sense fits. Cf. ⲡⲩⲧⲉⲕⲟ 'the prison' in accumulated vocabulary.

Four-fold passive/qualitative chain: 'they are bound (ⲭⲁⲗⲭ = ϫⲱⲗϫ̄), they are fettered (ⲙⲏⲣ qual.), they are blackened (ⲕⲙⲕⲁⲙⲧ̄ reduplicated of ⲕⲙⲟⲙ), they are buried (ⲧⲁⲙⲥ̄ = ⲧⲱⲙⲥ̄).' Each represents a discrete mode of archonic captivity in correspondential register.

Translated 'foundation/support' per accumulated vocabulary. Recurs lines 25, 29, 32 in 'foundation of the lions / of the man / of the First Man' — the cosmic-anthropological support upon which the archonic punishment-system rests.

Read as 'this little one now, the rivers being reckoned' — ⲡⲓⲕⲟⲩⲓ 'this little one' (small) + †ⲛⲟⲩ 'now' + ⲛⲓⲉⲣⲟ ⲏⲡ 'the rivers being counted.' The contrast between the diminutive earthly river and the cosmic river of Judgment (line 26: 'one out of a thousand') structures the passage.

notes.coptic_form: ⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲉⲣⲟ ⲅⲁⲣ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲱⲧ ϩⲛ̄ ϣⲟ ⲛ̄ⲗⲉⲣⲟ
notes.decision: 'For one river out of a thousand rivers' — ϣⲟ = 'thousand' (Coptic ϣⲟ). The exegetical formula contrasts the visible earthly river with the hidden cosmic-judicial multitude.

Tentatively read 'this multitude' (ⲡⲓ- + ⲁϣⲁⲓ̈ 'be many' + -ⲡⲉ copula). Context (god whose power holds the lions/archons) supports a quantitative-greatness term. Alternative reading 'this disgrace' (ⲡⲓ-ⲁϣⲓⲡⲉ from ϣⲓⲡⲉ 'shame') would yield 'this great disgrace within the power' — possible but less coherent with 'How great is that god.' Confidence low.
Translated 'the one which is exalted' — qualitative ⲟⲩⲁⲧⲃⲉ 'be exalted/lifted up' (cf. accumulated vocabulary). Modifies the troubled voice of wrath, contrasted (line 24) with thunders.

The line begins mid-discourse, completing the previous (lost) chapter. ϩϩⲃⲥⲱ read as ϩⲛ̄ϩⲃⲥⲱ 'garments' (or possibly just doubled ϩ); ⲛⲥⲉⲉⲗⲡⲉ tentatively parsed as ⲛ̄ⲥⲉ-(ⲣ̄)-ⲉⲗⲡⲉ 'and they hope' (Greek ἐλπίζω). The closing ⲛⲟⲩⲏⲣ ⲡⲉ is a Coptic copular question 'how much/long is it?' Translation kept literal and quizzical to reflect the obscurity.
